name: Arvada
seo_title: Arvada Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 8 Events, 1 Free
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Arvada, CO: the Olde Town tree lighting, Apex Park and Recreation District Santa and Grinch parties, Dickens Christmas and more.
lede: Arvada does Christmas around Olde Town Square, with a tree lighting, Santa visits and a winter market, while the Apex park district fills December Saturdays with Grinch parties, gingerbread and cookies with Santa.
celebrates: Arvada's holiday season centers on Olde Town, the historic square on Olde Wadsworth Boulevard, where Olde Town Arvada hosts an annual tree lighting and a series of holiday events. The City of Arvada hosts Winterfest in Olde Town Square, a free family event with games, performances, music, vendors and food. Apex Park and Recreation District adds Santa and Grinch programs at its recreation centers, and the Arvada Center for the Arts and Humanities puts on seasonal shows and a holiday art market. Local churches also host community Christmas events with crafts, music and photos with Santa.
lastyear: Christmas 2025 in Arvada centered on Olde Town Square. Olde Town Arvada hosted Saturdays with Santa on December 6, 13 and 20, from noon to 3 pm, and the host said every child who visited Santa received a complimentary cookie from Rheinlander Bakery. The Arvada Farmers Winter Market ran beside the Santa visits, with vendors selling handmade gifts, toys and local food. The City of Arvada also reports that Winterfest returned to Olde Town Square for a second straight year.
facts: Olde Town Arvada's holiday tree lighting reached its 21st annual edition in 2026, and the host opens the evening with a brass band march through the streets of Olde Town. Rheinlander Bakery, on Olde Wadsworth Boulevard, has supplied the cookies for children who visit Santa in the square. The RTD G Line commuter rail stops in Olde Town, so families can ride the train from Denver Union Station to the square. The Arvada Center for the Arts and Humanities is at 6901 Wadsworth Boulevard.
trains: Arvada has its own train stop. The RTD G Line commuter rail serves Olde Town Arvada, so families can ride from Denver Union Station to the square, and the tree lighting host suggests taking it on busy nights. For a heritage railroad outing, the Colorado Railroad Museum in Golden is a short drive south and west of Arvada, with its Santa and Polar Express style holiday rides. Our Golden page lists the current ride dates and ticket details.
train_links: Historic locomotives and cars, plus holiday train rides, a short drive from Arvada.
traditions: A brass band march, live music and the lighting of the tree in Olde Town Square mark the start of the season.
Santa has visited Olde Town Arvada Square on December Saturdays, with a cookie from Rheinlander Bakery for each child.
The City of Arvada's free family festival returned to Olde Town Square with games, performances, music and food.
The park district hosts Grinch parties, gingerbread building and cookies with Santa at its recreation centers.
The Arvada Center schedules seasonal stage shows and a holiday art market each winter.
kidfact: Kids can ride the G Line train to Olde Town Arvada, where Santa has handed out cookies from Rheinlander Bakery.
faq: Where do Arvada families go to see Santa?

Olde Town Arvada Square has hosted Saturdays with Santa on December Saturdays, with a free cookie from Rheinlander Bakery for each child who visits. The Apex Park and Recreation District also runs Santa programs at its recreation centers, including Cookies with Santa and a Special Time with Santa for individuals with disabilities. Each listing on this page has current details.
Is parking free in Olde Town Arvada?

The tree lighting host says parking in Olde Town is free, including the covered Olde Town parking hub on Vance Street. Event hosts also suggest taking the RTD G Line, which stops in Olde Town Arvada. Check the host's event page before you go, since street closures can change on busy holiday nights.
Who runs holiday programs for kids in Arvada?

The main hosts are Olde Town Arvada, the City of Arvada, Apex Park and Recreation District, and the Arvada Center. Apex posts Grinch parties, gingerbread building, cookies with Santa and winter bashes on its events calendar, and many programs require advance registration. Local churches also host free community Christmas events.
Can I take the train to Arvada for Christmas?

Yes. The RTD G Line commuter rail runs from Denver Union Station to Olde Town Arvada, so families can skip the parking and walk to the square. For a historic train ride, the Colorado Railroad Museum in Golden is a short drive away. See our Golden page for the museum's holiday ride listing and ticket details.
Are there free Christmas events in Arvada?

Yes. Winterfest is billed by the City of Arvada as a free family event, the Dickens Christmas Experience at Arvada United Methodist Church is free, and Saturdays with Santa in Olde Town has been free with a cookie for each child. Apex programs may charge or require registration, so check each host's page first.
